issues.legal_issue: Receipt of money under an executory agreement to grant a lease is not punishable where the lease never comes into existence.
material_facts: The appellants received money under an oral agreement to grant a lease of a flat in a building that was still under construction, with possession to follow completion.
The lease never came into existence; after completion, the building was requisitioned before the promised letting could take effect.
The appellants were prosecuted and convicted for receiving the money as a premium connected with the grant of a lease.
issues.conclusion: The receipt did not constitute an offence under section 18(1). The Court allowed the appeal, set aside the appellants’ convictions, and acquitted them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(1) refers to the grant, renewal or continuance of a lease, which contemplates a lease coming into existence; an executory promise to grant one is not itself a lease. Even giving “in respect of” its broad meaning of relating to or with reference to, the required relationship is to a lease, and the relationship of landlord and tenant arises only upon a demise of property capable of possession. Because the provision is penal, where two reasonable constructions are possible the construction that avoids imposing a penalty must be preferred, and the language must not be stretched beyond its fair and ordinary meaning. The Court relied on London and North Eastern Railway Co. v. Berriman (1946 AC 278, 295), and also noted that the statutory context and definitions of landlord and tenant supported its construction. The later addition of an exception for certain payments did not establish that the original provision covered executory agreements.

predicates.criminal_prosecution_for_receiving_money: A person was prosecuted for receiving money said to be connected with letting premises.
predicates.money_received_under_executory_lease_pro: A person received money under a promise to grant a lease in the future, rather than under a lease already in existence.

issues.definition: When a person is prosecuted for receiving money connected with letting, but received it under a future lease promise that never became a lease, the receipt is not punishable as a premium-receipt offence.
